idiom_name: Angular signal<T>/computed view-model + template bindings with reactive-context tracking
implementation_notes: Angular signals give the view-model typed observable state (signal<T>/WritableSignal), derived values as computed() (lazily evaluated and memoized), and template bindings that read signals inside a reactive context, so the framework knows exactly which views to re-render. Mutations go through .set()/.update(); exposing _count.asReadonly() keeps the writable source private. Strict templates type-check the view-model and the binding expressions, so most binding mistakes surface at compile time instead of as a blank control.
pitfalls: Signal reads outside a reactive context are untracked (subscriptions, lifecycle hooks): no dependency is created - use computed/effect deliberately.
Computed signals are lazy and memoized with reference equality: deriving from mutated arrays without replacing the signal value returns stale results.
Writable signals must stay private (asReadonly()) or consumers can set state behind the view-model's back.
Signals do not replace RxJS for event streams; mixing without bridging (toSignal) leaves views untracked.

variants.name: Vue 3 typed SFC reactivity
variants.idiom_name: Vue 3 <script setup lang="ts">: ref<T>/reactive<T> state + type-checked templates
variants.implementation_notes: Vue's typed composition API is the other typed binder: ref<T>()/reactive<T>() state, computed<T>() for derived values, defineProps/defineEmits for the component contract, and templates with lang="ts" whose binding expressions are type-checked by vue-tsc. The runtime is the same Proxy-based dependency tracking as plain Vue; the types make the view-model contract explicit so editors and builds catch mismatches that would otherwise fail silently at run time.
variants.code_sketch:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
const user = ref<string>('')
const canSubmit = computed<boolean>(() => user.value.trim().length > 0)
function submit(): void { api.login(user.value) }
</script>
<template>
  <input v-model="user" />
  <button :disabled="!canSubmit" @click="submit">Sign in</button>
</template>
pitfalls: Template type-checking requires vue-tsc; a Vite/esbuild-only build transpiles without checking, so template errors can ship.
Ref unwrapping differs between template and script: a ref nested in an object or array is not unwrapped in the template and renders as an object.
Typing reactive objects as broad generics erases the types of keys added later; prefer explicit interfaces plus refs.
withDefaults/props runtime declarations can drift from the type-level props, hiding required/prop-type mismatches from the checker.
